claim: Talos v1.14.5 is the latest stable release (published 2026-10-26); v1.15.0-beta.0 published 2026-11-10; tag v1.14.5 resolves to commit dad8d3ed
v1.14.5 release notes: Linux 6.18.58, etcd 3.7.3

Talos v1.14 support matrix: community support ends at the 1.15.0 release (2026-12-27, TBD); enterprise support offered by Sidero Labs; Kubernetes 1.33-1.37; NVIDIA drivers 595 (production) and 580 (LTS); amd64 and arm64 only

Official v1.14 SBC list: Banana Pi M64, Jetson Nano, Libre ALL-H3-CC, NanoPi R4S, Pine64, Rock64, ROCK Pi 4C, ROCK 4C+, ROCK 5B, Raspberry Pi 4B, CM4, Turing RK1, Orange Pi 5 (no Pi 5, no Jetson Orin)

All SBC ports are community-maintained and provided as-is; Sidero gives no official support for SBC boot, firmware or kernel issues; Raspberry Pi 5 appears only under unofficial ports (community talos-builder)

siderolabs/sbc-raspberrypi v0.3.0 (2026-11-02) ships rpi_5, rpi_generic and revpi_generic installers; Pi 5/CM5 device trees moved to the static RP1 topology for Linux 7.3; Pi 5 support first appeared in v0.1.8 (2026-01-26)

Image build: rootfs is packed into a SELinux-labelled squashfs, then placed with /init into a reproducible (SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH, sorted cpio --reproducible) zstd initramfs; the OS runs from RAM, there is no separate rootfs partition

imager builds every output (iso, disk image, installer, kernel, initramfs, UKI, cmdline) from one profile: overlay first, then initramfs rebuilt with system extensions, kernel args, then a UKI signed with separate Secure Boot and PCR signers

Image Factory schematic = YAML (overlay, extraKernelArgs, META values, systemExtensions, bootloader, secureboot, disk image); schematic ID is the sha256 of its canonical form; Factory publishes a cosign public key
Image Factory core is MPL-2.0; its enterprise/ folder (SBOM, VEX, scanner, attestation, tokens) is BSL 1.1 with no Additional Use Grant, change date 2030-11-03 to MPL-2.0

Disk layout: partitions EFI, BIOS (GRUB legacy), BOOT (GRUB mode, holds A and B kernel+initramfs), META, STATE (machine config), EPHEMERAL (containerd, pods, etcd data; fills the disk), optional IMAGECACHE

Docs: upgrades use an A-B scheme retaining the previous kernel and OS image; if an upgrade fails to boot Talos rolls back; if Talos boots but workloads fail the operator must run talosctl rollback; upgrades are API-driven and scheduling is left to the user's own logic
Upgrade sequence: denyNewServices, cordon+drain, stop pods, pre-shutdown, stop containers and services, unmount, then run installer; installer writes META tag 'Upgrade' = previous boot label

Automatic revert: when the machined boot sequence returns an error, handle() calls revertBootloader, which reads the META 'Upgrade' tag and flips the bootloader default back to the previous label, then reboots; with no tag nothing is reverted
Commit point: DropUpgradeFallbackController deletes the META 'Upgrade' tag once MachineStatus is Stage=Running and Ready, once per boot
Ready = time synced + network (address, connectivity, etc files, hostname) + services apid, machined (+kubelet; +etcd and trustd on control plane) + static pods Ready + Kubernetes Node Ready
NodeReady is copied from the Node object's Ready condition with no check of heartbeat freshness

GRUB mode: rollback flips Default/Fallback between BootA and BootB labels in grub.cfg; sd-boot (UEFI/Secure Boot) mode keeps the booted UKI as Fallback, deletes older UKIs and writes the new UKI plus EFI variables
Manual rollback API (MachineService/Rollback) flips the bootloader and reboots; Rollback, Upgrade and Reset require role os:admin

Issue #14260: after upgrading v1.13.8 to v1.14.0 a USB-boot node landed in maintenance mode (no config, no network); the reporter rolled back to v1.13.8 by hand; cause: USB storage drivers became modules in the kernel config
Issue #14000: upgrading v1.13.7 to v1.13.8 left state in EPHEMERAL that broke Longhorn attach on 3 control-plane nodes; rolling Talos back did not fix it; only wiping EPHEMERAL did
Issue #14061 (open): talosctl rollback returns success immediately without waiting for health, unlike talosctl upgrade; duplicate of #7337 closed as not planned
Issue #14002 (fixed 2026-08-23): sd-boot upgrade could keep the old persistent default as rollback target and delete the UKI actually running after a manual menu selection

System extension manifest = version, name, version, author, description, compatibility.talos.version (semver constraint); validation rejects world-writable and special files and any path outside an allow-list (/etc/cri/conf.d, /usr/lib/firmware, /usr/lib/modules, glibc loader, ldconfig, nvidia-modprobe, /usr/local, ...)

Extension services: host daemons run as containers defined by YAML (name, container entrypoint/env/mounts/security, depends on service/path/network/time/configuration, restart policy); the Tailscale extension mounts /dev/net/tun and state dirs and depends on cri + network

Official extensions catalog includes NVIDIA (nonfree kmod, OSS modules, container toolkit, fabric manager, production/lts), Hailo (hailort), Rockchip RKNN, AMD/Intel NPU, Tenstorrent, ZFS, iSCSI, DRBD, Tailscale, NetBird, ZeroTier, Nebula, gVisor, Kata, RevPi firmware, NUT client; no NATS, ROS or CAN-bus extension

Kubernetes components are not in the OS image: kubelet is pulled as ghcr.io/siderolabs/kubelet and etcd as registry.k8s.io/etcd; default Kubernetes 1.37.1, 6 supported versions; an OS upgrade does not upgrade Kubernetes by default
Identity: single declarative gRPC API with mutual TLS; roles os:admin, os:operator, os:reader, os:etcd:backup, os:image:verifier, os:meta:writer, os:impersonator; no SSH and no shell
Disk encryption key options: static (weakest), nodeID (protects only removed drives), kms (network KMS), tpm (strong when paired with SecureBoot)
SELinux is experimental: enabled by default since 1.10 in permissive mode; enforcing tested only with the default Flannel CNI
Backup story is etcd only: talosctl etcd snapshot on a healthy control plane, scheduled snapshots recommended; recovery bootstraps from the snapshot; no host/app data backup in the OS

System requirements: control plane min 2 GiB / 2 cores / 10 GiB (recommended 4 GiB / 4 / 100 GiB); worker min 1 GiB / 1 / 10 GiB (recommended 2 GiB / 2 / 100 GiB); x86_64 needs microarchitecture level 2+
AI features are documentation-side only: llms.txt, a skill.md for Claude Code and a remote MCP server at docs.siderolabs.com/mcp exposing the docs; no on-node AI or agent API
Talos AI contribution policy (2026-09-18): AI-generated issues/PRs and bot or agent submissions are not accepted
Talos is MPL-2.0 (LICENSE at tag)

Omni is BSL 1.1; Additional Use Grant covers only non-production use, testing and home-lab personal use; any environment a business depends on needs a commercial licence; change date 2030-10-23 to MPL-2.0

Pricing: community edition free (MPL-2.0); Talos Enterprise Linux $1,000/node/year, 10-node minimum, includes Omni, FIPS 140-3 builds, SBOM+VEX, CVE SLAs, indemnity, 24/7; Omni Hobby free (10 nodes, 2 users), Startup $25/node/month (50 nodes), Edge tier 'contact us'
Vendor page: Omni schedules containers directly on Talos at single-node edge sites with no Kubernetes cluster
Talos Enterprise Linux: FIPS 140-3 Go module (CMVP #5247) in every build from 1.13; per-schematic SPDX 2.3 SBOM; VEX; scan reports; served from factory.siderolabs.com
ADOPTERS.md lists 16 organisations, mostly cloud/on-prem clusters; two edge-device users: SCHULZ Systemtechnik (IoT and ML edge devices) and Vandebron (energy edge devices)
